ety.text: From Middle English valve, from Latin valva (“double door, valve”). Doublet of valva.

senses.d: A device that controls the flow of a gas or fluid through a space, such as a pipe, manifold, or plenum.
ex: open the valve

senses.d: Such a device that admits fuel and air into the cylinder of an internal combustion engine, or one that allows combustion gases to exit.
ex: Near-synonym: poppet valve

senses.d: One or more membranous partitions, flaps, or folds, which permit the passage of the contents of a vessel or cavity in one direction, but stop or control the flow in the opposite direction.

senses.d: The quality that renders something desirable or valuable; worth.
ex: There is tremendous value in a good education.
An abacus is of little value when you have an electronic calculator.

senses.d: The degree of importance given to something.
ex: The value of my children's happiness is second only to that of my wife.

senses.d: That which is valued or highly esteemed, such as one's morals, morality, or belief system.
ex: He does not share his parents' values.
family values

senses.d: The amount (of money or goods or services) that is considered to be a fair equivalent for something else.
ex: The value of the stolen painting is estimated to be around four million pounds.
His design was not to pay him the value of his pictures, because they were above any price.

senses.d: The relative duration of a musical note.
ex: The value of a crotchet is twice that of a quaver.

senses.d: The relative darkness or lightness of a color in (a specific area of) a painting etc.
ex: When pigments of equal value are mixed together, the resulting color will be a darker value. This is the result of subtraction.
Shadows and light move very quickly when you are painting on location. Use Cobalt Blue to quickly establish the painting's values.

senses.d: Any definite numerical quantity or other mathematical object, determined by being measured, computed, or otherwise defined.
ex: The exact value of pi cannot be represented in decimal notation.

senses.d: Precise meaning; import.
ex: the value of a word; the value of a legal instrument

senses.d: The valuable ingredients to be obtained by treating a mass or compound; specifically, the precious metals contained in rock, gravel, etc.
ex: The vein carries good values.
the values on the hanging walls

senses.d: Esteem; regard.
ex: The French have a high value for them ; and I confess they are often what they call delicate
My relation to the person was so near, and my value for him so great.

senses.d: To determine or estimate the value of; to judge the worth of.
ex: I will have the family jewels valued by a professional.
The property has been valued at six million pounds.

senses.d: To regard highly; think much of; place importance upon.
ex: Gold was valued highly among the Romans.
I value his advice.

senses.d: To hold dear; to cherish.
ex: I value these old photographs.
